critique: The note proves an exact Kneser-based variance identity, the degree-one positive-density correction, an if-and-only-if CR2 ratio-consistency condition, and a same-class impossibility result for uniformly estimating exact variance. It does not prove a Gaussian limit, valid studentization, Wald coverage, an optimal conservative variance estimator, or an extension beyond homogeneous fixed group size, which limits its practical inferential reach and leading-journal significance. The sparse theorem's justification and consumer prose nevertheless say that experiments obtain "justified CR2 inference," which overstates variance-estimator ratio consistency in the absence of any distributional or coverage theorem and should be replaced by "justified CR2 variance estimation." Supporting evidence is confined to one eight-unit enumeration, so the package does not establish how often or how severely the dense correction matters in realistically sized designs.
